subject: Model-fit probe: acceptance thresholds & benchmarks (post-demo)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@bluehaven.ai>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@bluehaven.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model-fit probe: acceptance thresholds & benchmarks (post-demo)

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Short follow-up with the bits we agreed to surface so the team can evaluate fit more concretely. High level: we think there are two sensible paths for BlueHaven based on the demo signals — a lower-latency open-model stack (quantized Llama-3 candidate) vs a tuned proprietary baseline (customer-tuned checkpoint). Each path has different acceptance criteria and operational tradeoffs, so below are concrete artifacts and a suggested evaluation plan.

Quick ask: can you confirm who on your side will run the acceptance checklist (engineering or ML infra)? That will determine whether we send the prompt bundle or a lightweight API harness.

What I attached / linked:
- prompt_bundles_bluehaven_v1.zip — a focused set of 120 prompt families derived from your demo transcripts (classification, slot-filling, follow-up generation).
- benchmark_summary_v1.csv — token-level latency/cost estimates for the two candidate stacks on 8xA100 and 4xH100 configs.
- mops_canary_checklist.md — suggested canary metrics and rollback gates.

Suggested acceptance thresholds (initial):
- Precision@K (entity extraction) >= 0.92 on the holdout prompt set
- Response correctness (human eval pass rate) >= 0.88 at 95% confidence
- Average 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for short-turn prompts (<=128 tokens)
- Token cost per 1k outputs not to exceed your target of $6 (we can tune batching/quantization)

Immediate next steps (owner):
1) Elena: confirm evaluation owner and preferred infra (your cluster vs Redwood sandbox) — due Wed 2027-06-09.
2) Tom / Eng: if you want the API harness, we can ship a containerized test client by EOD Tue.
3) Marissa / Karthik: we’ll circle back with a recommended model list + canary parameter presets by Tue evening.

Concerns we flagged in the demo that matter for parity:
- Prompt sensitivity on multi-turn clarifications (we saw repeat hallucination on address normalization examples).
- Out-of-distribution entity formats (international phone / postal variants) where the open models showed variance.

I’ll attach the prompt set now and follow with a short companion note recommending three candidate models and a runbook for quick evals.

Thanks —
Soojin 
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Model-fit probe: acceptance thresholds & benchmarks (post-demo)

Perfect — noted that Elena will own evals. Answers inline and sending the prioritized assets.

Priority prompt slices (run order):
1) Clarification sequence (20 prompts) — captures the multi-turn address/normalization pattern you highlighted.
2) Entity extraction (30 prompts) — high-precision cases + edge OOD formats.
3) Response scoring (30 prompts) — pairwise human-eval candidates for correctness.
4) Latency stress (40 short prompts) — synthetic low-latency workload for p95 measurements.

Candidate models we recommend for initial parity runs (we’ll pre-configure recommended quantization & KV cache settings):
- open-1: Llama-3-20B-q4f (open candidate) — best low-cost latency tradeoff; needs prompt engineering for hallucination sensitivity.
- open-2: Mistral-8x-quant (open candidate) — strong few-shot generation, slightly heavier on tokens for entity consistency.
- prop-1: Redwood-Tuned-Baseline-11B (proprietary baseline) — we’ve historically seen higher entity precision after light fine-tune but higher cost; good for a control baseline.

Benchmark links and artifacts: 
- Candidate-run summary (html): https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/reports/bh-benchmarks-20270607.html
- Raw csv (attachment): benchmark_summary_v1.csv
- Prompt bundle (attachment): prompt_bundles_bluehaven_v1.zip

Quality regression concerns & mitigations:
- If open candidate shows >5% drop in entity precision vs baseline, we recommend a prompt bundle augmentation step (30 targeted calibration prompts) before any fine-tune.
- Canary gating: require randomized human eval on 200 examples with interleaved baseline + candidate; fail if candidate < baseline - 0.04 in mean correctness.

Operational notes for the sandbox run:
- Data: use synthetic PII masks; do not upload real PII during initial parity runs.
- Retention: sandbox logs will be retained for 14 days (we can increase if you want auditability).
- Access: we’ll provision a scoped API key limited to your evaluation project.

Next actions (to keep momentum):
- Today EOD: I’ll share the canary checklist (mops_canary_checklist.md) and a 1-page runbook for your eng team.
- Tue: Marissa / Karthik will drop recommended canary parameter presets (batch size, KV cache warm-up steps, quant settings).

Thanks — sending attachments now.

Soojin
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: benchmark_summary_v1.csv, mops_canary_checklist.md]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 20:05:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: canary presets + notes for BlueHaven run

Internal note (not to forward):

High-level presets I recommend for the first parity sweep (we can revise after the first 500 queries):
- Llama-3-20B-q4f: batch_size=8, kv_warmup=16 steps, soft_prompting_off, sampling: top_p=0.92 temp=0.0, pad_to=128
- Mistral-8x-quant: batch_size=6, kv_warmup=12, top_p=0.95 temp=0.0, postprocess: entity-normalizer v1.3
- Redwood-Tuned-Baseline-11B: batch_size=10, kv_warmup=8, soft_prompting_on, temp=0.0

Canary gates (operational):
- Gate A (safety): no outputs with obvious PII pass-through in 500-sample random check.
- Gate B (quality): human-eval mean correctness delta >= -0.04 vs baseline for initial rollout.
- Gate C (latency): p95 <= 450ms on Redwood sandbox (we can tighten once in your infra).

Action items:
- Soojin: confirm these presets in the runbook and add to the container entrypoint.
- Karthik: prepare quick scripts to compute Precision@K and aggregated human-eval scoring and push to the shared Drive.

Tagging the hubspot deal (BH-20270607-01) and will attach a short summary after first run.

Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
